edit.explain.motion: Both links pinned to the frame can only swing over limited arcs. The coupler is the shortest link and can turn fully relative to them, so each rocker stops at a toggle where the coupler lines up with the other one. Here the input is driven from 24.2° to 87°, a swing of 62.9°: at 24.2° the coupler is in line with the input rocker and the output stops at 54.9°, and at 87° the input is 1.9° short of its own toggle at 88.9°, where the coupler lines up with the output rocker. Between these ends both rockers move one way, and the output swings 69.6°, from 54.9° to 124.5°.
edit.explain.forces: The coupler carries push or pull only. Near the input's toggle the coupler comes into line with the output rocker: the transmission angle reaches 159° and the input cannot drive past 88.9°. At the output toggle the coupler is in line with the input rocker, the transmission angle falls to 31°, and a load on the output cannot turn the input back.
edit.ratio.typical: input swing 62.9° (24.2° to 87°) gives output swing 69.6° (54.9° to 124.5°) with defaults
edit.build.defining_relations: Grashof s + l <= p + q (60 + 100 = 160 <= 180) with the shortest link as coupler gives a Grashof double rocker. Input toggles where |O4A| = c ± b (11.5° and 88.9°); output toggle where |O2B| = a + b (output 54.9° at input 24.2°). B = circle(A, b) ∩ circle(O4, c).
edit.build.range: input rocker driven 24.2° to 87° (62.9°), from the output toggle to 1.9° inside the input toggle at 88.9°; output rocker 54.9° to 124.5° (69.6°), one way per input stroke
edit.build.notes: Drive the input from the output toggle (24.2°, coupler in line with the input rocker) to just inside the input toggle (88.9°, coupler in line with the output rocker). Between these two toggles both rockers move one way, so the output's extremes fall at the ends of the input stroke. Driven over the whole range between the input toggles (11.5° to 88.9°) the output would reverse partway through. Stay on one branch.

review.note: Applies the 2026-10-19 review (rethink) and the issue's decisions: a wheel on each knuckle, dashed wheel-axis lines and the rear-axle line that meet near one point, the turning centre. The wheelbase is shortened from 250 to 200 mm and the arms lengthened from 30 to 45 mm. The left knuckle keeps its range of -30 to +40 degrees; to reach -30 the arms are angled 18.5 degrees inward, a little less than the 20.6 degrees that aims them at the rear axle centre, and the outer wheel stays within 2 degrees of the ideal over the whole range. A shorter wheelbase would put the centre nearer but cannot reach -30 degrees with a good trapezoid. R1 (#212), 2026-10-22: reviewed again on the finished v3 build (six phases, PLAN and an angled view): rethink, as decided. A wheel stands on each knuckle on a stub axle in an upright tube (stub 24 mm, width 18, so the wheel clears its tube); the wheel axis lines are carried to the rear axle line and the turning centre is marked where they meet, about 38 mm behind that line at full lock because the outer wheel turns 1.5 degrees more than ideal. The base holds the rear axle line and both full-lock centres. The tie rod closes on the right side of the dyad, which the record had reversed.

overlays.label: ARMS AIM NEAR THE REAR AXLE CENTRE

claims.text: outer wheel 23.9° at inner 30° (ideal 21.9°), about 0.80 x inner

edit.explain.motion: Each front wheel steers about its kingpin on a knuckle with a steering arm. The arms point inward, roughly at the centre of the rear axle, and are joined by a tie rod, forming a trapezoid. When one wheel steers, the tie rod turns the other wheel by a smaller angle on the outside of the turn, so the two wheel axis lines meet near one point on the rear axle line, the turning centre.
edit.ratio.typical: outer angle about 0.80 x inner angle at 30° (23.9° vs 30°)
edit.build.ground: front axle beam with kingpins KL (-75,0) and KR (75,0); rear axle line at y = -200
edit.build.defining_relations: Ideal Ackermann: cot(delta_outer) - cot(delta_inner) = w / L = 0.75. Arms angled inward by beta = 18.5°, a little less than atan((w/2)/L) = 20.6°, which would aim them at the rear axle centre, so the tie rod still reaches the -30° lock. Tie rod t = w - 2 r sin(beta) = 121.4 mm.
edit.build.range: left knuckle -30° to +40° (right turn to left turn); right knuckle -43.5° to +28.8°. Outer wheel 9.3°, 17.3°, 23.9°, 28.8° at inner 10°, 20°, 30°, 40° (ideal 8.9°, 16.0°, 21.9°, 27.3°)
edit.build.notes: Tie rod behind the axle: PR = circleX(KR, r, PL, t, +1). A wheel on each knuckle, on a stub axle 24 mm outboard of the kingpin, carried by an upright tube round the kingpin. Draw both wheel axis lines and the rear-axle line dashed: they meet near one point, the turning centre, which lies on the plate at full lock (about 300 mm to the side).
